title: Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Chorus Personnel
tiers.description: All Directors, officers and employees of Chorus who intend to deal in Chorus Restricted Securities. Subject to the fundamental no-dealing-on-Inside-Information rule and the short term dealing guidance, but not to Schedule 1's black-out periods, consent-before-dealing requirement or hedging ban unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors of Chorus, the Chief Executive, all members of the senior management team, all direct reports to senior management, anyone managing a principal function of Chorus, all members of the Financial Controllers Team, and anyone else designated (permanently or temporarily) by the General Counsel and Company Secretary. Subject to Schedule 1's Additional Rules: black-out periods, prior consent before dealing, and the hedging ban on unvested at-risk remuneration.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of Restricted Persons; every dealing additionally requires the Chairman of the Board's approval (as does any Restricted Person's dealing exceeding 100,000 shares/options), and additional disclosure requirements apply (see the Additional Disclosure Requirements for Directors and Officers).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse, children, other relatives, associates, trusts of which the person is a trustee, or companies the person controls. The Policy applies to any dealing the person is involved or instrumental in, whether or not the securities are held in their own name or an associate's, and a controlled trust or company's dealing while the person has Inside Information is deemed procured by that person.

definitions.hedging_definition: A Restricted Person shall not enter into any transaction (including any hedging or derivative transaction) which will limit that person's economic risk in relation to such unvested shares, options or rights [issued or acquired under any future Chorus employee incentive schemes where performance hurdles have not yet been achieved or other conditions have not yet been met].

windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the release of half-year results to the NZSX and ASX

windows.start_anchor: Chorus's year end balance date (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the release of full-year results to the NZSX and ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The General Counsel and Company Secretary may determine other black-out periods for Restricted Persons from time to time (e.g. prior to release of a prospectus for a general public offer of Chorus shares).

rules.detail: 'Chorus Restricted Securities' expressly include derivatives and other financial products created over Chorus securities. Chorus Personnel who are not Restricted Persons may deal in them without any consent process, provided they hold no Inside Information; the base Policy has no clearance regime for this tier.
rules.evidence: "Chorus Restricted Securities" means any Chorus shares, options, derivatives and debt securities. ... any other securities of Chorus and any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any securities of Chorus.

rules.detail: Entering an OTC derivative over Chorus shares is a dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security requiring prior notification and consent from the General Counsel and Company Secretary; also requires the Chairman's approval if the dealing involves a Director or exceeds 100,000 shares/options.
rules.evidence: Notify the General Counsel and Company Secretary of your intention to deal in Chorus Restricted Securities and seek consent to do so ... all dealings involving (i) Chorus Directors or (ii) greater than 100,000 shares/options must be approved by the Chairman of the Board.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging or any derivative transaction limiting economic risk in 'at-risk' remuneration, meaning unvested shares/options/rights under a future Chorus employee incentive scheme where performance hurdles or other conditions are not yet met.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements to limit their exposure in relation to "at-risk" remuneration ... A Restricted Person shall not enter into any transaction (including any hedging or derivative transaction) which will limit that person's economic risk in relation to such unvested shares, options or rights.

rules.detail: The Schedule 1 hedging ban is expressly addressed only to Restricted Persons; the base Policy has no equivalent hedging prohibition for other Chorus Personnel.

The hedging ban (cl.18) is expressly limited to unvested 'at-risk' remuneration. Hedging fully vested, unrestricted shares is not separately prohibited; it is an ordinary dealing in Chorus Restricted Securities requiring consent.
rules.evidence: Notify the General Counsel and Company Secretary of your intention to deal in Chorus Restricted Securities and seek consent to do so

rules.detail: No hedging-specific rule and no consent regime apply to this tier; hedging vested shares is only subject to the fundamental no-dealing-on-Inside-Information rule.
rules.evidence: "deal" includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of Chorus Restricted Securities or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. An agreement to dispose of shares in future is a 'deal'; for this tier only the Inside Information rule applies, with no consent process.
rules.evidence: "deal" includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of Chorus Restricted Securities or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent.

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar arrangement is 'otherwise dealing' in Chorus shares and requires prior consent.
rules.evidence: Otherwise deal in Chorus shares (e.g. gifting shares to a family member or transferring shares to a trust).

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

A CFD referencing Chorus shares is a 'financial product ... created over or in respect of' Chorus securities, so is a Chorus Restricted Security; for this tier only the Inside Information rule applies.
rules.evidence: any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any securities of Chorus

rules.detail: Same consent process as any other dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security.
rules.evidence: Notify the General Counsel and Company Secretary of your intention to deal in Chorus Restricted Securities and seek consent to do so

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

Secured financing arrangements are not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. Transferring shares to a collateral agent to secure a loan is not addressed, though the analogous example of 'transferring shares to a trust' is treated as a dealing requiring consent for Restricted Persons, suggesting a similar transfer to a lender/custodian would likely be treated the same way.
Buying and selling within a 3 month period should be avoided unless exceptional circumstances are discussed with, and approved by, the General Counsel and Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: You should not engage in short term dealing (i.e. buying and selling Chorus Restricted Securities within a 3 month period) unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved by the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Once dealing is complete, this must be disclosed')
clearance.evidence: Consent to deal, if it is granted, will be provided by way of letter, fax or email. A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification ... A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the Restricted Person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.

clearance.approver: General Counsel and Company Secretary, and the Chairman of the Board
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Once dealing is complete, this must be disclosed')
clearance.evidence: all dealings involving (i) Chorus Directors or (ii) greater than 100,000 shares/options must be approved by the Chairman of the Board.

short_term.evidence: You should not engage in short term dealing (i.e. buying and selling Chorus Restricted Securities within a 3 month period) unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved by the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

exceptions.evidence: The Restricted Person is in severe financial hardship.
The Restricted Person is required by a court order or other court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell Chorus Restricted Securities.
Acquire Chorus shares through the vesting of your restricted shares under any future Chorus Restricted Share Scheme.
Cease contributions to any future Employee Share Scheme because you are in possession of Inside Information.
Cease to participate in any future DRP because you are in possession of Inside Information.
Consent is also not required should your restricted shares, options or rights (zepos) granted under any future Chorus employee incentive scheme lapse or be forfeited.

exemption_authority: The General Counsel and Company Secretary may grant a specific exemption from a black-out period in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, or a court order/enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell) (Schedule 1, cl.4), and may approve dealing outside those circumstances for short-term dealing (main Policy, para 18). All dealings by Directors, or by any Restricted Person exceeding 100,000 shares/options, additionally require the Chairman of the Board's approval (Schedule 1, cl.8).

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested at-risk remuneration
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements to limit their exposure in relation to "at-risk" remuneration (meaning any unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under any future Chorus employee incentive schemes where performance hurdles have not yet been achieved or other conditions have not yet been met).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by the only hedging-specific prohibition in the Policy; it is treated as an ordinary dealing requiring consent (for Restricted Persons) or nothing beyond the Inside Information rule (for other Chorus Personnel).

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Chorus Restricted Securities" means any Chorus shares, options, derivatives and debt securities. ... any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any securities of Chorus.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no interpretive gap: entering an OTC put/call collar is unambiguously a dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security, so the consent process (for Restricted Persons) applies directly rather than by analogy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, or encumbering securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither banned nor expressly permitted; the Bank should confirm with the General Counsel and Company Secretary whether pledging or transferring the shares to a collateral agent needs consent as an 'otherwise deal[ing]' in Chorus shares, by analogy with the express 'transferring shares to a trust' example.

bespoke_clauses.topic: double approval for Directors and large trades
bespoke_clauses.clause: all dealings involving (i) Chorus Directors or (ii) greater than 100,000 shares/options must be approved by the Chairman of the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar, or any Restricted Person's collar exceeding 100,000 shares/options, needs both General Counsel and Company Secretary consent and separate Chairman approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification ... A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the Restricted Person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar must occur within 10 trading days of consent, and any inside information arising before execution voids the consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies whether the dealing is to be done in New Zealand or overseas and whether or not the dealing relates to Chorus' New Zealand or foreign securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An offshore-booked OTC collar with an international bank is still squarely within scope of the Policy and its consent/black-out requirements.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Chorus shares appears achievable. The Policy's only hedging-specific prohibition is expressly limited to unvested 'at-risk' remuneration, so hedging vested shares is treated as an ordinary dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security (a category that expressly includes derivatives): for a Restricted Person this needs prior written consent from the General Counsel and Company Secretary (plus Chairman approval if the person is a Director or the trade exceeds 100,000 shares/options), consent lasting 10 trading days and lapsing automatically if Inside Information arises, executed outside the two annual results black-out periods (or any ad hoc GC&CS-declared period) absent severe hardship or a court order; for other Chorus Personnel, only the fundamental no-dealing-on-Inside-Information rule applies, with no consent process at all. The Policy is entirely silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so the loan leg of the collar is not expressly addressed either way, and the Bank should confirm whether pledging the shares or transferring them to a collateral agent is treated as 'dealing' requiring the same consent, given the Policy's example that transferring shares to a trust does require consent. As a dual NZX/ASX-listed issuer, the Policy applies to dealings anywhere in the world, so an offshore-booked collar is not outside its scope.
